create.name: Vedanta Center of Greater Washington, D.C.
create.bio:
Silver Spring's Vedanta Center of Greater Washington, D.C. belongs to the Ramakrishna Order and sits in Maryland on a wooded plot of about two and a half acres just north of the capital. Swami Swahananda of the Vedanta Society of Southern California opened it in April 1997 in the brick house that came with the land. A worship hall and monks' quarters followed in 2000, and a domed temple housing a marble figure of Ramakrishna was dedicated in 2013. Swami Atmajnanananda is minister in charge, with Swami Bhaswatananda as his assistant.

The centre teaches Vedanta through the lives and words of Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi and Swami Vivekananda, and welcomes anyone who wants to deepen a spiritual life, whatever their background. The shrine is open from early morning to evening for quiet meditation, with arati at dawn and dusk. Its weekly round includes a Sunday lecture, guided meditation sessions, classes on the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna and on texts such as the Pancadasi, some held on Zoom, together with karma yoga work days, retreats and festivals. Talks are streamed and archived on its YouTube channel, and an audio library on its site keeps Sunday lectures going back more than a decade.

free_resources.title: Audio Lectures
free_resources.description: A long archive of Sunday talks by Swami Atmajnanananda, listed by date from the early 2010s, on subjects from the Song of the Sannyasin to the mystery of maya. Each can be played on the page.

free_resources.title: Video Lectures
free_resources.description: The centre's page of featured recorded discourses from its Sunday programme, played from its YouTube channel.

free_resources.title: Monthly Programme and Daily Worship
free_resources.description: The month's letter of talks, festivals and visiting monks, alongside the daily shrine hours with dawn and evening arati followed by silent meditation, open to anyone.
